'''Thomas Weiland''' (born 24 October 1951) is a German [[electrical engineer]], [[physicist]] and [[Entrepreneurship|entrepreneur]]. He is a [[professor]] of electrical engineering and headed the Institute of Electromagnetic Field Theory at the [[Department of Electrical Engineering and Information Technology of TU Darmstadt|Department of Electrical Engineering and Information Technology]] of the [[Technische Universität Darmstadt|Technical University of Darmstadt]] from 1989 to 2017. In 1988, Weiland was awarded the [[Leibniz Prize|Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Liste der mit dem Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz-Preis Ausgezeichneten |url=https://www.dfg.de/download/pdf/gefoerderte_projekte/preistraeger/gwl-preis/uebersicht_leibniz_preistraeger.pdf#page=13 |access-date=2023-06-21 |website=Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG) |language=de}}</ref> He was also named an [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]] Fellow in the year 2012, for development of the [[finite integration technique]] and impact of the [[computational electromagnetics|associated software]] on [[electromagnetic]] engineering.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=March 12, 2012 |title=MTT Society News: Newly elevated fellows |journal=IEEE Microwave Magazine |publisher=IEEE |volume=13 |issue=2 |pages=94–95 |doi=10.1109/MMM.2011.2181670 |issn=1557-9581 }}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Thomas Weiland was born on 24 October 1951 in [[Riegelsberg]], which was then a part of [[Saar Protectorate]].<ref name=":02"/> From 1961 to 1970, he attended the Ludwigsgymnasium in [[Saarbrücken]].<ref name=":03">{{Cite web |title=Staff at TEMF {{!}} Prof. Dr.-Ing. Thomas Weiland |url=https://www.temf.tu-darmstadt.de/team_temf/mitarbeitende_temf/mitarbeitende_details_6744.en.jsp |access-date=2023-06-21 |website=Institute for Accelerator Science and Electromagnetic Fields (TEMF) |publisher=Technical University of Darmstadt}}</ref> His thirst for research became apparent early on here, as he received six mathematics and physics prizes at state and national level while still a student. This also included several successful participations in the ''[[Jugend forscht]]'' program, which was already very popular at the time.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1968 |title=Tonmodulierte Hochfrequenz als Signalträger elektronisch chiffrieren und dechiffrieren |url=https://www.jugend-forscht.de/projektdatenbank/tonmodulierte-hochfrequenz-als-signaltraeger-elektronisch-chiffrieren-und-dechiffrieren.html |access-date=2023-06-21 |website=jugend forscht {{!}} Projektdatenbank |publisher=Stiftung Jugend forscht e. V. |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=1969 |title=Mathematisch-elektronisches Chiffriersystem zur geheimen Nachrichtenübermittlung |url=https://www.jugend-forscht.de/projektdatenbank/mathematisch-elektronisches-chiffriersystem-zur-geheimen-nachrichtenuebermittlung.html |access-date=2023-06-21 |website=jugend forscht {{!}} Projektdatenbank |publisher=Stiftung Jugend forscht e. V. |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=1970 |title=Entwicklung und Bau eines billigen Präzisions-Frequenzmessers sowie einer automatischen Oszillographenschaltung |url=https://www.jugend-forscht.de/projektdatenbank/entwicklung-und-bau-eines-billigen-praezisions-frequenzmessers-sowie-einer-automatischen-oszillographenschaltung.html |access-date=2023-06-21 |website=jugend forscht {{!}} Projektdatenbank |publisher=Stiftung Jugend forscht e. V. |language=de}}</ref> After being accepted into the [[Friedrich Ebert Foundation]]'s study sponsorship program, Weiland studied at the [[Technische Universität Darmstadt|Technische Hochschule Darmstadt]] (TH Darmstadt) beginning in 1970. He graduated there in 1975 with a [[diploma]] in Theoretical Electrical Engineering.<ref name=":03" />

== Scientific career ==
As a [[research assistant]] at the Chair of Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering, Thomas Weiland remained in TH Darmstadt for the next four years after receiving his diploma. In the meantime, he received his [[doctorate]] in [[engineering]] in 1977. In 1979, he joined the Theory Group at the [[CERN]] particle laboratory in Switzerland as a fellow. From 1981, he worked as a research associate at the [[DESY]] research center in [[Hamburg]] and headed the Electromagnetic Fields Group there from 1982 to 1989.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |title=Die Mitglieder der Akademie und der Jungen Akademie {{!}} Prof. Dr.-Ing. Thomas Weiland |url=https://www.adwmainz.de/mitglieder/profil/prof-dr-ing-thomas-weiland.html |access-date=2023-06-21 |website=Akademie der Wissenschaften und der Literatur Mainz |language=de}}</ref> In parallel, he led the [[Plasma acceleration#Wakefield acceleration|Wakefield Accelerator]] Research Group and here he was able to eventually prove the wakefield transformation – which was previously invented by himself and G.A. Voss – with his wakefield experiment in 1987.<ref>Voss, G. A. & Weiland, T. (April, 1982). [https://bib-pubdb1.desy.de/record/224393/files/IR-DESY-M-82-10.pdf "Particle acceleration by wake fields"] [Internal report No. M-82-10, unpublished]. [[DESY|''Deutsches Elektronen-Synchrotron (DESY)'']], Hamburg, Germany: pp. 1-21. [https://bib-pubdb1.desy.de/search?cc=InternalReport&ln=en&jrec=89&sf=year&p=weiland ''DESY Publications Database''], retrieved 2023-06-27.</ref><ref>Voss, G. A. & Weiland, T. (1982). [https://lss.fnal.gov/conf/C8209271/p287.pdf "The wake field acceleration mechanism"] [Conference paper]. [https://lss.fnal.gov/conf/C8209271/ ''Proceedings of the ECFA-RAL topical meeting: The challenge of ultra-high energies''], invited. Oxford, England, September 27–30, 1982: pp. 287–308. [https://lss.fnal.gov/ ''Fermilab Technical Publications''], retrieved 2023-06-27.</ref><ref>Bialowons, W., Bremer H. D., Decker, F. J., Lewin, H. C., Voss, G. A.,  Schütt, P., Weiland, T. & Xiao C. (1987). [http://cds.cern.ch/record/182997/files/CERN-87-11-V-1.pdf#page=308 "The wake field transformer experiment at DESY"] [Conference paper]''.'' [http://cds.cern.ch/record/182997/files/CERN-87-11-V-1.pdf ''ECFA - CAS/CERN - IN2P3 - IRF/CEA - EPS workshop on new developments in particle acceleration techniques''] [Conference report, October 12, 1987]. S. Turner (ed.). Vol. 1. Orsay, France, June 29 - July 4, 1987: [http://cds.cern.ch/record/182997/files/CERN-87-11-V-1.pdf pp. 298-307]. [http://cds.cern.ch/record/182997?ln=de ''CERN document server''], retrieved 2023-06-27.</ref> Also within this period, Weiland completed his [[habilitation]] in [[experimental physics]] at the [[University of Hamburg]] (1984).<ref name=":02" />

Furthermore, in the first half of the 1980s Weiland was a visiting scientist at scientific institutions in the U.S. and Japan several times, including [[Stanford University]]. Subsequently, he turned down several offers of professorships in Texas and Berlin, taking over as chair of Electromagnetic Field Theory at the TH Darmstadt (later renamed TU Darmstadt) in 1989  – a position he held until 2017. In 1994 and 1997, he spent two [[sabbatical]]s at Stanford University and the [[University of Victoria]].<ref name=":03"/>

Starting in 2000, Weiland, together with several other professors at the TU Darmstadt, pushed a comprehensive [[computational engineering]] initiative.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=GSC 233: Graduate School of Computational Engineering |url=https://gepris.dfg.de/gepris/projekt/39112826?language=en |access-date=2023-06-22 |website=GEPRIS - Geförderte Projekte der DFG |publisher=Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft}}</ref> From 2003 to 2006, he was [[chairman of the board of directors]] of the Computational Engineering Research Center, which had been newly established the year before.<ref name=":02" /> In 2007, the founding of the ''Graduate School of Computational Engineering'' (Graduate School CE) followed as part of the Excellence Initiative of the German federal and state governments.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Graduate-School-CE |url=https://www.ce.tu-darmstadt.de/graduate_school_ce/index.en.jsp |access-date=2023-06-22 |website=Computational Engineering at the Technical University of Darmstadt}}</ref>

In the course of his time as professor and head of his institute at the TU Darmstadt, Thomas Weiland guided over 100 doctoral students to a successful doctorate. In turn, ten professorships emerged from the circle of these. Together with his staff, Weiland published almost 1400 scientific publications.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Publications - Thomas Weiland |url=https://tubiblio.ulb.tu-darmstadt.de/view/person/Weiland=3AThomas=3A=3A.html |access-date=2023-06-22 |website=TUbiblio |publisher=Technical University of Darmstadt}}</ref>

== Scientific work ==
Weiland's research focuses on the development of [[computational electromagnetics|numerical methods for the computation of electromagnetic fields]], with applications in [[electromagnetic compatibility]], [[accelerator physics]], [[computational engineering]] (computer-aided modeling, simulation, analysis and optimization), [[Time domain|time domain analysis and simulation]], as well as [[Multiphysics simulation|multiphysics simulation methods]] and [[problem solving]].

Weiland had already dealt with the numerical computation of electromagnetic fields in the course of his doctorate. This was not only to shape his own career. Particularly a few years later, it should revolutionize the general approach to prototype construction within electrical engineering and have a lasting influence on it to this day. A central position of Weiland's calculations and his scientific work is occupied by his development of the [[finite integration technique]] (FIT). He first presented this in 1977, as a consistent formulation for the discrete representation of [[Maxwell's equations|Maxwell's basic electromagnetic equations]] on spatial grids. Finite Integration Theory (also known as Finite Integration Technique) forms the physical-mathematical basis of simulation programs that are currently almost indispensable in the development of a wide range of technological products, such as [[mobile phone]]s.<ref>Weiland, Thomas. "A discretization model for the solution of Maxwell's equations for six-component fields''"'' (1977)''.'' ''International Journal of Electronics and Communications'' (former ''[[AEU: International Journal of Electronics and Communications|AEÜ - Archiv für Elektronik und Übertragungstechnik]]''). Hirzel. Volume 31, Issue 3: pp. 116-120. [[ISSN (identifier)|ISSN]] [https://www.worldcat.org/de/search?q=n2:1434-8411 1434-8411]</ref><ref name=":04">{{Cite web |last=Johnston |first=Hamish |date=May 26, 2009 |title=Electromagnetic software accelerates ahead |url=https://physicsworld.com/a/electromagnetic-software-accelerates-ahead/ |access-date=2023-06-27 |website=Physics World |publisher=IOP Publishing}}</ref>

== Entrepreneurship and economic importance ==
In order to be able to use the results of his basic electromagnetic research for concrete [[technical development]]s, Weiland began in 1985 to bundle his scientific findings with regard to FIT in what was then a new type of software: ''MAFIA'' ('''Ma'''xwell's Equations by the '''F'''inite '''I'''ntegration '''A'''lgorithm), a [[Computer-aided design|CAD system]], prepared by an international collaboration between DESY, [[Forschungszentrum Jülich|KFA Jülich]] and [[Los Alamos National Laboratory|LANL]] which had been initiatively set up by Weiland, quickly proved to be groundbreaking. It allowed electromagnetic fields and their interactions to be modeled and simulated [[three-dimensionally]], automatically and so realistically on the computer that time-consuming experiments or tests during prototype construction became largely superfluous.<ref>Weiland, Thomas (1985). [https://bib-pubdb1.desy.de/record/275762/files/DESY-M-85-08-T-Weiland-Computer-Modelling.pdf "Computer modelling of two- and three-dimensional cavities"] [Conference paper]. ''11th Particle Accelerator Conference: Accelerator Engineering and Technology.'' Vancouver, Canada, May 13–16, 1985: pp. 1-5. [https://bib-pubdb1.desy.de/search?cc=InternalReport&ln=en&jrec=89&sf=year&p=weiland ''DESY Publications Database''], retrieved 2023-06-27.</ref><ref>Klatt, R., Krawczyk, F., Novender, W. R., Palm, C. & Weiland, T. [DESY], Steffen, B. [Kernforschungsanlage Jülich], Barts, T., Browman, M. J., Cooper, R., Mottershead C. T., Rodenz, S.G. [Los Alamos National Laboratory] (1986). [https://bib-pubdb1.desy.de/record/275743/files/DESY-M-86-07-R-Klatt-et-al-MAFIA.pdf "MAFIA - a three-dimensional electromagnetic CAD system for magnets, RF structures, and transient wakefield calculations"] [Conference paper]. ''13th International Linear Accelerator Conference,'' Stanford, USA, January 2–6, 1986: pp. 14-16:  [https://bib-pubdb1.desy.de/search?cc=InternalReport&ln=en&jrec=89&sf=year&p=weiland ''DESY Publications Database''], retrieved 2023-06-27.</ref><ref name=":04" />

For continuous development and commercial distribution of his software, Weiland founded Computer Simulation Technology GmbH (CST) in 1992. CST GmbH operated in the sector of electromagnetic field simulation in the time domain, with offices in 16 countries. In 1998, the algorithms of the MAFIA software were re-embedded into CST Microwave Studio and in 2005 into the CST Studio Suite software package. Companies in various industries (such as the Bosch Group, Airbus Defence & Space, or Dentsply Sirona) use this software based on the Finite Integration Technique to reduce development effort, costs, and time to market for new products.<ref name=":04" /><ref name=":12">{{Cite journal |last=Ludwig |first=Astrid |date=July 17, 2018 |title=Millionenspenden als Dank für akademische Freiheit |journal=Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung |language=de |issue=163 |pages=32 |issn=0174-4909}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=October 3, 2016 |title=Dassault Systèmes Completes CST Acquisition |url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20161002005036/en/Dassault-Syst%C3%A8mes-Completes-CST-Acquisition |access-date=2023-06-27 |website=Business Wire}}</ref>

In the year 2008, CST GmbH was converted into an ''[[Aktiengesellschaft]]'' in which Weiland acted as chairman of the [[supervisory board]] until 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Firmenbekanntmachungen {{!}} CST - Computer Simulation Technology GmbH, Darmstadt |url=https://www.northdata.de/CST+-+Computer+Simulation+Technology+GmbH,+Darmstadt/HRB+96826 |access-date=2023-06-27 |website=North Data |language=de}}</ref> In the fourth quarter of 2016, CST AG became part of [[Dassault Systèmes|Dassault Systèmes SE]] and was thus integrated into Europe's second-largest software group after [[SAP]]. Dassault Systèmes saw the integration of the CST solutions into its existing [[Computer-aided design|CAD applications]] as a forward-looking opportunity to set a new industry standard: for [[Multiphysics simulation|multiphysics]] and [[Multiscale modeling|multiscale simulation]] of [[Vehicular automation|autonomous vehicles]], networked buildings, medical equipment, [[Electronic devices|wearable electronic devices]], [[smartwatch]]es and [[E-textiles|smart textiles]] as well as many other objects within the [[Internet of things|Internet of Things]].<ref name=":2" />

Additionally, Weiland founded in 2014 Advanced Computational Engineering GmbH (ACE) together with other [[shareholder]]s. ACE advises companies on the application of computational engineering methods and on related project development and study preparation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Firmenbekanntmachungen {{!}} ACE - Advanced Computational Engineering GmbH |url=https://www.northdata.de/ACE+-+Advanced+Computational+Engineering+GmbH,+Gr%C3%BCnwald/Amtsgericht+M%C3%BCnchen+HRB+253734 |access-date=2023-06-27 |website=North Data |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=ACE GmbH - About |url=https://ace-gmbh.biz/en/about |access-date=2023-06-30 |website=ace-gmbh.biz}}</ref> Since 2017 he has been chairman of the supervisory board of ALCAN Systems GmbH which is active in the development of [[liquid crystal]] flat panel [[smart antenna]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Firmenbekanntmachungen {{!}} ALCAN Systems GmbH, Darmstadt |url=https://www.northdata.de/ALCAN+Systems+GmbH,+Darmstadt/HRB+95752 |access-date=2023-06-27 |website=North Data |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=ALCAN Systems {{!}} About - Board members |url=https://www.alcansystems.com/about/ |access-date=2023-06-27 |website=ALCAN Systems |language=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=ALCAN the smart antenna company |url=https://www.alcansystems.com/ |access-date=2023-06-27 |website=ALCAN systems}}</ref>

== Social commitment and Thomas Weiland Foundation ==
Weiland himself is well aware of the importance of the TU Darmstadt (former TH Darmstadt) in terms of his scientific and entrepreneurial career. He sees it as a place of [[autonomy]] and flexibility that allows scientists an extraordinary degree of freedom in both teaching and research – and to which, in his own words, he would like to "give something back" accordingly.<ref>Thomas Weiland in his concluding remarks on honoring the new scholarship holders at the Georg Christoph Lichtenberg House in Darmstadt on July 9, 2022 [unpublished].</ref><ref name=":12" /> With this in mind, following the sale of CST AG in 2016, he provided the university with a sum for a new building.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 19, 2016 |title=TU Darmstadt erhält neues Institutsgebäude |url=https://www.welt.de/regionales/hessen/article160435403/TU-Darmstadt-erhaelt-neues-Institutsgebaeude.html |access-date=2023-06-27 |website=DIE WELT |language=de}}</ref>

Enabling young people to study and supporting university students, respectively, is also a very special concern of his. The Thomas Weiland Foundation, which he established 2014, therefore rewards excellent school and study achievements. It currently supports around 50 bachelor's and master's students (and around 20 new ones each year) with a [[scholarship]] that largely covers living expenses throughout their studies. In 2021, an additional funding line was created for prize winners of ''Jugend forscht''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Thomas Weiland Foundation |url=https://www.tu-darmstadt.de/thomas-weiland-stiftung/die_stiftung/vorstellung/index.en.jsp |access-date=2023-06-27 |website=TU Darmstadt - Thomas Weiland Foundation}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Saß |first=Karl Ulrich |date=April 21, 2022 |title=Stipendien für kluge Köpfe und forschende Jugend: Thomas Weiland-Stiftung erweitert Stipendienangebot |url=https://www.tu-darmstadt.de/universitaet/aktuelles_meldungen/archiv_2/2022/2022quartal2/news_archiv_de_363328.de.jsp |access-date=2023-06-27 |website=TU Darmstadt - News Archiv |language=de}}</ref>
